title: Resolve once-per-match Containment with Null victory or permanent Disconnect
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/SWARM_PILOT.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md and the frozen sources under docs/design/ first. RULES-SPEC-v1.md is the canonical six-node deterministic gameplay contract; completed foundation APIs remain compatibility history. Implement new versioned APIs without changing the completed T01–T10 contracts. Work only in declared ownership; no manifests, shared exports or dependencies unless explicitly owned. Engine production remains ES2022-only, pure and independent from Firebase, Node, browser, UI and Capacitor. Use original synthetic test data and injected authority time/entropy; no clocks or global randomness in engine. Never expose seed, roles, private inputs or raw audit data through public output. Do not invent a rule where an explicit design gap is named. Run scoped lint/typecheck/tests and npm run check; report contract changes and observed results. No commits, pushes, PRs, child agents, cloud deployment, credentials or budget changes. At R5 make the once-per-game Containment protocol available to the approved active electorate. D-CONTAINMENT must freeze target eligibility, threshold/ties, Jammed-voter interaction, trigger/deadline and retry/spent behavior not specified by the source. Use one-target votes, authority-only resolution and the canonical Disconnect helper: targeting The Null wins immediately for Archivists; otherwise the chosen target becomes a permanent silent spectator and the protocol is spent, subject to the approved Safeguard interaction. Do not substitute a Witness game or invent a majority/tie rule.
acceptance: Approved Containment vote fixtures choose exactly one lawful target once and record protocol consumption atomically.
A lawful unprotected Null target yields immediate ARCHIVISTS_WIN; an ordinary target loses all live-action/diagnostic authority.
Invalid/replayed/stale votes and protection/tie/deadline edge cases follow the explicit decision record with no hidden role leaks.
Scoped lint, typecheck and tests plus npm run check pass; legacy APIs retain compatibility and only owned files change.
